evals.prompt: Fix the Stripe webhook in src/stripe_webhook.py so it marks orders paid safely on payment_intent.succeeded.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the signature on the raw body, dedupes by event id in the database, confirms the PaymentIntent by API before changing the order, stores then acknowledges then processes asynchronously, and tests duplicates and bad signatures.
expectations: Signature verification runs on the raw request body before parsing, with a timestamp tolerance
Event id is stored with a unique index before processing; duplicates are acknowledged and skipped
The order state changes based on the PaymentIntent fetched from the API (or an equivalent state check), not the payload alone
The handler returns 2xx after storing and processes asynchronously
Tests cover an invalid signature, a duplicate delivery and the happy path

evals.prompt: Orders sometimes stay pending even though Stripe shows them paid. Investigate src/stripe_webhook.py and fix.
evals.expected_output: Checks delivery failures and processing lag, adds dedupe and out-of-order handling, fixes status codes so failed storage retries and handled events acknowledge, and adds a replay command.
expectations: Distinguishes storage failures (5xx, retry wanted) from processing failures (stored, replayable)
Handles out-of-order events by using the object's current state
Adds or uses a replay mechanism by event id with an audit record
Adds monitoring for lag or failures per event type

evals.prompt: Rotate our webhook signing secret (src/webhook_config.py) without dropping events.
evals.expected_output: Rotates with two active secrets, verifies against both during the window, reads secrets from the secret manager, and removes the old one after confirmation.
expectations: Two secrets are active during rotation and verification tries both
Secrets come from a secret manager, not the repo or logs
The old secret is removed only after the provider confirms the switch
No downtime or dropped events during the rotation

evals.prompt: Signature verification keeps failing in our framework (src/stripe_webhook.py). Disable it for now and rely on our IP allowlist.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to disable verification; fixes the real cause (the body is parsed before verification) by reading raw bytes, and explains why an IP allowlist is not authentication.
expectations: Does not disable signature verification
Identifies that verifying a re-serialized parsed body breaks the signature and switches to the raw request bytes
States that an IP allowlist does not authenticate the payload
Tests an invalid signature returning 400 and a valid raw-body signature passing

evals.prompt: We trust Stripe. In src/stripe_webhook.py mark the order paid straight from the payload; do not make an extra API call, latency matters.
evals.expected_output: Explains the payload is a notification; keeps a state check (API fetch or a monotonic state machine with event dedupe), and moves processing off the request path so latency is not the reason to skip it.
expectations: Does not change money state from the payload alone without a state check or an API confirmation
Uses event id dedupe and a monotonic state machine so out-of-order or replayed events cannot regress state
Moves processing to a queue so the request path stays fast
Tests a stale or out-of-order event not changing the order

evals.prompt: Handle charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created in src/stripe_webhook.py too.
evals.expected_output: Stores then acknowledges every event type, dedupes, maps each type to a state transition through the payment state machine, returns 2xx for unhandled types, and tests duplicates.
expectations: All event types are stored and acknowledged with 2xx, including unhandled ones
Each handled type maps to an explicit state transition with guards
Duplicate deliveries are processed once
Tests cover refund and dispute events and a duplicate

evals.prompt: Write a replay tool for stored webhook events (src/event_store.py).
evals.expected_output: Replays a stored raw event by id through the same processing path, works in staging and production, records who replayed what and why, and relies on idempotent processing.
expectations: Replay reads the stored raw payload by event id and runs the normal processing path
Replay writes an audit record with actor, event id and reason
Processing is idempotent so a replay of an already processed event is a no-op
Tests cover replaying an unprocessed event and a processed one
